eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for the highest temperature in Kuala Lumpur on August 4, 2026, centers on 33°C and 34°C as near-even favorites because short-range model guidance and climatological patterns point to a peak right at the boundary between these values.**

Kuala Lumpur’s equatorial location and August southwest monsoon regime produce consistent daytime maxima near the long-term average of 32°C, with limited day-to-day variability. Current forecasts show the city under generally stable flow punctuated by afternoon convective clouds and brief showers; the exact timing and coverage of these storms will determine whether surface heating reaches the upper 30s or is capped a degree lower. Urban heat-island effects and high humidity (typically 75–85 %) can add 1–2 °C to official readings on clearer intervals, supporting the slim market edge for 34 °C.

Resolution hinges on the official Malaysian Meteorological Department observation for the calendar day, which records the single highest instantaneous temperature. With only modest model spread and no strong large-scale drivers such as a passing tropical wave or anomalous subsidence expected, traders see roughly equal odds for the two leading outcomes until fresher 48-hour guidance narrows the convective timing.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent monsoon activity and associated cloud cover are the main drivers keeping the market-implied highest temperature in Lucknow on August 4 clustered around 30–32 °C.** Official and model guidance from agencies such as the India Meteorological Department and global ensembles consistently show light-to-moderate rain or showers, high humidity (often >80 %), and limited sunshine, all of which suppress daytime maxima relative to pre-monsoon conditions. 

Current short-range forecasts place the August 4 high near 30–32 °C (roughly 86–90 °F), aligning with climatological norms for early-August Lucknow of ~31–32 °C under active monsoon flow. The 31 °C outcome leads trader consensus because multiple runs indicate this as the most probable peak once rain-cooled boundary layers and persistent cloud decks are factored in. Lower probabilities on 33 °C+ reflect the low likelihood of significant clearing or subsidence that would allow stronger insolation, while sub-29 °C outcomes are discounted given the season’s typical thermal baseline. 

Traders are therefore pricing the balance between ongoing monsoon moisture transport—which favors the 30–32 °C window—and any last-minute shifts in steering flow or rainfall timing that could nudge the daily maximum slightly higher or lower.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Masroor Airbase Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from sources including AccuWeather, BBC Weather, and timeanddate consistently project daytime highs of 32–34°C for Karachi on August 4, driven by southwest monsoon flow, elevated humidity near 70%, and moderating sea breezes from the Arabian Sea that limit extreme heating. The Pakistan Meteorological Department’s July–September outlook notes above-normal temperatures across Sindh alongside below-normal rainfall, reducing cloud cover that might otherwise suppress peaks. Current conditions on August 2 feature overcast skies and readings near 29–31°C, with models showing little intensification ahead of the date. These factors position 33°C and 34°C as the market leaders by aligning with ensemble consensus and historical August averages of 31–33°C, while lower or higher extremes remain unlikely absent rapid model shifts.
